story.value: Curium was first produced in 1944 by Glenn T. Seaborg, Ralph A. James and Albert Ghiorso.
The first curium was made by striking plutonium atoms with alpha particles that were sped up in a device called a cyclotron.
Curium was the third transuranium element to be discovered.

uses.value: Curium is mainly used for basic scientific research.
Curium currently has no commercial uses.
Curium might be used in radioisotope thermoelectric generators in the future.
Curium compounds, like the element itself, are mainly used for basic scientific research.
